ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are two horizontal solenoids very close to each other. The left solenoid is connected in a closed circuit, and below the circuit there is a variable resistor R_Left and a battery; in the battery symbol, the long plate on the left is the positive terminal, and the short plate on the right is the negative terminal. The right solenoid is connected in another closed circuit, with a resistor R_right on the right and an ammeter at the bottom. The winding directions of the two solenoids are drawn in the figure as having the same handedness. Reasoning: In the left circuit, conventional current starts from the positive terminal of the battery, passes through R_Left and enters the left end of the left solenoid, then flows along the solenoid winding toward the right end, and finally returns to the negative terminal of the battery. Judging by gripping the solenoid with the right hand according to the winding direction in the figure, the right end of the left solenoid is the north pole and the left end is the south pole, so at the right solenoid, the direction of the magnetic field produced by the left solenoid points to the right. Now R_Left slowly increases, so the current in the left circuit decreases, and the rightward magnetic flux passing through the right solenoid decreases. According to Lenz's law, the induced current in the right circuit must produce a magnetic field in the same direction, that is, it must also produce a rightward magnetic field to oppose the decrease in magnetic flux. For the right solenoid, using the right-hand rule with the same winding direction, to produce a rightward magnetic field, the induced conventional current should flow along the right solenoid from the left end to the right end, then downward through the right resistor, and return from right to left through the ammeter. Therefore the direction of conventional current indicated by the ammeter corresponds to the needle deflecting to the left.

method.method_draft: Use a magnetic-pole/Lenz-law route. First read the diagram: the left circuit contains a battery, variable resistor R_left, and a solenoid; the right circuit contains a nearby solenoid, resistor R_right, and an ammeter. Note the battery polarity in the left circuit and trace the conventional current through the left solenoid. From the drawn winding sense, apply the right-hand grip rule to identify the magnetic polarity/field direction produced by the left solenoid at the nearby right solenoid. From the text, use that increasing R_left slowly decreases the left-circuit current, so the magnetic flux through the right solenoid due to the left solenoid is decreasing. By Lenz’s law, the induced current in the right circuit must create a magnetic field in the same direction as the original weakening field. Apply the right-hand grip rule to the right solenoid’s winding to get the required induced conventional current direction in the right circuit, then map that current direction through the ammeter symbol to the indicated needle deflection. This gives a leftward deflection.

图像描述：图中有两个相距很近的水平螺线管。左侧螺线管接在一个闭合电路中，电路下方有可变电阻 R_Left 和电池；电池符号中左边长极板为正极、右边短极板为负极。右侧螺线管接在另一个闭合电路中，右边有电阻 R_right，底部有一个安培表。两只螺线管的绕向在图中画成相同的手性。
推理：左侧电路中，常规电流从电池正极出发，经 R_Left 进入左侧螺线管的左端，再沿螺线管绕组流向右端，最后回到电池负极。按图中绕向用右手握螺线管判断，左侧螺线管右端为北极，左端为南极，因此在右侧螺线管处，由左侧螺线管产生的磁场方向指向右方。现在 R_Left 缓慢增大，所以左侧电路电流减小，穿过右侧螺线管的向右磁通量减小。根据楞次定律，右侧电路中的感应电流必须产生同方向的磁场，即也要产生向右的磁场来阻碍磁通量的减小。对右侧螺线管按同样绕向使用右手定则，要产生向右磁场，感应常规电流应沿右侧螺线管由左端流向右端，然后经右侧电阻向下，并通过安培表从右向左返回。因此安培表所指示的常规电流方向对应针向左偏转。

method.method_draft: Use a transformer/dot-convention sign route. From the image, treat the two close solenoids as magnetically coupled coils and assign corresponding dotted ends by comparing the winding sense of the left and right solenoids as drawn. Trace the conventional current in the left circuit from the battery polarity to decide whether the primary current enters or leaves its corresponding dotted end. From the text, increasing R_left means the primary current magnitude is decreasing. Apply the coupled-inductor rule equivalent to Faraday-Lenz law: when current entering a dotted primary terminal decreases, the induced secondary emf has the polarity that would drive current so as to support the original flux. Using the dot assignment and the right-hand circuit wiring, determine the resulting conventional current through the ammeter. Interpreting the ammeter’s indicated current direction gives a deflection to the left.

Image description: In the figure there are two horizontal solenoids very close to each other. The left solenoid is connected in a closed circuit, and below the circuit there is a variable resistor R_Left and a battery; in the battery symbol, the long plate on the left is the positive terminal, and the short plate on the right is the negative terminal. The right solenoid is connected in another closed circuit, with a resistor R_right on the right and an ammeter at the bottom. The winding directions of the two solenoids are drawn in the figure as having the same handedness.
Reasoning: In the left circuit, conventional current starts from the positive terminal of the battery, passes through R_Left and enters the left end of the left solenoid, then flows along the solenoid winding toward the right end, and finally returns to the negative terminal of the battery. Judging by gripping the solenoid with the right hand according to the winding direction in the figure, the right end of the left solenoid is the north pole and the left end is the south pole, so at the right solenoid, the direction of the magnetic field produced by the left solenoid points to the right. Now R_Left slowly increases, so the current in the left circuit decreases, and the rightward magnetic flux passing through the right solenoid decreases. According to Lenz's law, the induced current in the right circuit must produce a magnetic field in the same direction, that is, it must also produce a rightward magnetic field to oppose the decrease in magnetic flux. For the right solenoid, using the right-hand rule with the same winding direction, to produce a rightward magnetic field, the induced conventional current should flow along the right solenoid from the left end to the right end, then downward through the right resistor, and return from right to left through the ammeter. Therefore the direction of conventional current indicated by the ammeter corresponds to the needle deflecting to the left.

Reasoning trace is consistent with the image, the standard answer, and the assigned dot-convention/Faraday-Lenz method. Minor improvement: explicitly state that the ammeter/needle convention being used is that conventional current through the meter from right to left corresponds to a left deflection, since this final mapping is somewhat implicit.

In which direction does the ammeter needle (indicating the direction of conventional current) in the right-hand circuit deflect in response to this change?
